Text.Text: Roberta Bakewell, Master of Domestication
Bakewell is often assumed to understand the language of animals better than that of humans. But of course this is only half the story.
Alfreda Nobel, Highly Skilled Explosives Manufacturer
For Nobel, quality means that her explosives detonate when they are supposed to. Not before and not after.
Otto Nicolaus Deutz, Father of the Modern Internal Combustion Engine
It is thanks to Deutz's urge to research that there are vehicles and machines today that have more than one horsepower.
Ludmilla Burberry, Manufacturer of the Finest Fabrics
Burberry has a special feel for the fibers of her fabrics and in her career she has woven together like every type of them, always with the most perplexing result for the Haute Couture.
Edison A. Thomas, Vorstand von Tungsram Inc.

Thomas leads his international conglomerate of companies with an iron fist, always looking for new ways to exploit his clients and maximizing his personal profit share for his patented carbon filament, knowing that his technology is already outdated.
Konrad Krupp, Foundry Champion
Krupp is not afraid of getting its own fingers dirty and often checks in person to what extent his steel products meet the highest quality standards.
Princess Sibilla Camci, Master of Reflection

Although princess Camci comes from a tradition-conscious and exceedingly conservative noble family of the eastern kingdoms, she has farsightedly recognized that only fair and equal treatment of workers can bring the best results.
Dr. Möbius Merk, Alchemist by Conviction
Dr. Merk does not believe in the formulas of modern science but follows his very own instincts, firmly convinced that gold can be made from base metals. He is very close!
Johannes Becker, First Industrial Master Miller
With his revolutionary inventions, Becker played a decisive role in industrial food production.
Juan-Franco de Esposito, Sucrose Expert
De Esposito has visited countless universities in the old world and has soaked up every knowledge of the processing and refining of various types of plants.
Otto van der Wiel, Bone Crusher by Principle
Van der Wiel sees himself as the most important cog in the food chain, because at the end of the day someone has to lead the remains to a higher purpose.
Helmuth Sauerbruch, The Molecular Whisperer
Sauerbruch never trusted charts nor textbooks. Instead, he listens—quite literally—to the fumes, the hisses, the pulses of his vats. He says chemistry talks to those willing to inhale its secrets.
